Read-only requests to the Senate's Open Legislation API at the moment you ask. The Senate receives the legislative data from the Legislative Bill Drafting Commission (LBDC) in a raw file format, and Open Legislation cleans it up before publishing it through the API. Needs NYS_LEGISLATION_API_KEY (a free key from the Senate); a server without one cannot reach this source.

Reshaped by BetaNYC (values unchanged): Passed on as the API returns it, with three additions that change no value: the paging totals the API puts beside a list of results are copied in with the results, each bill gets a link to its page on nysenate.gov, and each law document gets a link to the law on nysenate.gov.

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Committees, committee meetings, floor calendars, agendas and floor transcripts are the Senate's only. The Senate does not say how far back each kind of data goes. Caveat: Bill text, status, votes and law text are official legislative data but may be corrected or amended later. Check anything important at legislation.nysenate.gov. Caveat: Dates and times in the API's answers are New York local time, written without a time zone. Caveat: When this server also has a local copy (topic corpus), most tools answer from that copy first and ask the API only when the copy has nothing. An answer from the copy says so and gives the date it was last synced.

Built on your own machine, not shipped in the package: this repository's scripts download the data from the Open Legislation API (scripts/fetch-data.js once, then scripts/sync.js to pick up changes, both with an API key) and save each item's JSON as the API returned it. Each sync asks for the changes since the last one ended, in New York time as the API expects, and records when it ended. The server then reads that copy with no network call.

Reshaped by BetaNYC (values unchanged): Each item is the API's own JSON, saved and read back unchanged, with a note on each answer giving the time the copy was last synced. search_members adds each member's chamber and full name, taken from the Senate's own records: the full name is the one on the member's most recent sponsored bill, used for every session, because the member list does not carry it.

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Committees, committee meetings, floor calendars, agendas and floor transcripts are the Senate's only. The Senate does not say how far back each kind of data goes. Known gap: The copy starts at the session year chosen when it was built (2009 unless the person who built it chose otherwise), and is only as current as its last sync. Known gap: Committees are not picked up by the sync, because the API's change feed does not carry them; they are as current as the last full download. Known gap: Law text and transcript text are in the copy only if it was built with them, and are not picked up by the sync. Without them, those tools ask the live API, or, with no API key, say the item is not in the copy. Known gap: A member who has never been the prime sponsor of a bill in the copy has no full name in it. Known gap: Lists answered from the copy have no total count; only the live API gives one. Known gap: A copy last synced by a version before 2.7.0 can be missing changes made in the hours after each of its syncs, and during its first download. Running the sync once from the date the copy was built picks them up (see What's changed). Caveat: Not found in the local copy is not the same as does not exist: the copy may not have synced that item. With an API key, an empty answer from the copy is checked against the live API. Caveat: Without an API key, this copy is the only data the server has, and it may be out of date.
